spec_family.name: New Construction Wainscot Panel System Painting
spec_family.description: Combined prime+paint spec for wainscot panel assemblies in new construction. Covers the entire panel system below the cap rail as a single SF-based item: panels, internal rails, stiles, base rail, and applied molding. Wainscot_type (flat_panel, raised_panel, beadboard) drives production rate complexity modifier. Substrate-driven primer selection for bare substrates; primer conditional on substrate_state (SS_BARE requires primer, SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips to finish). QT-driven finish systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Cap rail excluded — handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT. Material systems are QT-driven recommendations — contractor retains discretion.

includes: Wainscot panel face priming and painting (flat, raised, or beadboard panels)
Internal framing painting (rails, stiles within the wainscot assembly)
Base rail painting (bottom horizontal frame member)
Applied molding painting (decorative molding within assembly)
Surface prep per substrate (sanding, dust removal, MDF edge sealing)
Wainscot-to-wall junction caulking (assembly perimeter where it meets drywall)
Cap-rail-to-panel junction caulking (prep from panel side)
MDF edge sealing with solvent-based sealer (bare MDF only — step 1 of two-step prime)
Primer coat — conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE
Finish coat application (spray or brush) — 2 coats standard, 3+ at QT5 brush per FFD §15.10.3
Between-coat interstage process (inspect, sand, repair, clean) at ALL quality tiers
Floor protection at wainscot work zone base
Wall masking above cap rail line (spray method only)

excludes.item: Cap rail (wainscot top rail) — LF-based trim item
Baseboard below wainscot — LF-based trim item
Wall field above wainscot — drywall painting

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, repair scope, and coat count. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers). Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 not applicable — wainscot is prominent, scrutinized millwork per Millwork Doctrine §6. QT3=standard production. QT4=premium (full sand, systematic inspect). QT5=superior (thorough sand, critical inspect, 3+ coats brush). Sheen/QT gate enforced at runtime.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for primer and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray preferred for NC production — large flat panels spray efficiently. Brush for occupied spaces, small areas, or touch-up. Spray requires wall masking above cap rail line.

configuration_dimensions.description: Panel construction type. Drives production rate complexity modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: flat_panel=baseline (standard flat panels with simple frame). raised_panel=1.25× time modifier (3D profile with detail edges, more cutting-in). beadboard=1.15× (uniform vertical grooves requiring additional attention). Modifiers from Millwork Doctrine §7.2. Beadboard 1.15× is interpolated (doctrine has standard 1.0× and complex 1.25×).

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish sheen. Constrained by quality tier gate.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin default for softer wainscot appearance. QT3+satin is a compatible default (no tension). Semi-gloss available at QT4+. Gloss at QT5 only.

configuration_dimensions.description: Input substrate condition. Drives primer requirement and prep scope.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_BARE: full primer coat required (substrate-driven chemistry), heavier prep (full sand). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, lighter prep (scuff sand only). Standard NC wainscot arrives pre-primed from mill.

paintable_items.name: Wainscot panel assembly
paintable_items.counting_rules: Measure total SF of wainscot panel assembly below cap rail. Includes panels, internal rails/stiles, base rail, and applied molding. Measured as wall area covered by wainscot system. Sourced from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING. Internal framing complexity captured by wainscot_type modifier — no separate LF item for framing.
paintable_items.notes: Single SF item. Standard wainscot height 32-42 inches. Always H1 (1.0× — no access equipment needed). Raised panel adds ~10% effective surface area over measured wall SF due to 3D profile.

variants.notes: Most common NC scenario. Factory-primed, standard spray production. No primer — scuff sand then 2 finish coats. Fastest production variant.
Factory-primed, superior spray. QT5 spray uses 2 coats (not 3). Full protection.
Factory-primed, standard brush. No wall masking needed. 2 finish coats.
Factory-primed, superior brush with gloss. 3 finish coats per FFD §15.10.3.
Bare substrate, standard spray. Primer + 2 finish coats. Full protection.
Bare substrate, premium spray. Primer + 2 finish coats.
Bare substrate, superior brush with gloss. Primer + 3 finish coats. 4 total coats, 3 interstage cycles.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Total SF of wainscot panel assembly below cap rail. Measured as wall area covered by wainscot system. Includes panels + internal framing + base rail + applied molding.
Floor protection area at wainscot work zone base. Drop cloth runners.
Wall masking LF above cap rail line for spray method.

protection_zones_required.notes: Canvas drop cloth runners at base of wainscot work area. Wainscot is low to floor — drip protection and sanding dust control.
Paper + tape masking above cap rail line to protect wall from overspray. Spray method only.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Wall field above wainscot meets at cap rail line. Different finish — wall paint (flat/eggshell) vs millwork enamel (satin/semi-gloss). Junction at cap rail, which is handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.
Cap rail at top of wainscot. Same finish group typical. Cap rail handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (ITM_TRIM_WAINSCOT_RAIL). Same session painting typical — no masking needed.
Standard baseboard below wainscot. Often same finish group. Baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (ITM_TRIM_BASEBOARD).
Wainscot meets door casing where both present in same wall. Complex intersection — panels terminate at casing edge. Typically same finish group.
Wainscot meets window casing where windows are within wainscot height zone. Complex intersection. Typically same finish group.

valid_input_states.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE requires full primer coat (substrate-driven chemistry). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer — lighter prep only. Standard NC delivery is factory-primed.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen dimension. Satin is default.

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished walls need no protection during brush application. Typical NC scenario — walls may still be bare when wainscot is painted.
Spray method requires wall masking even on unfinished walls to prevent overspray.
When walls are finished (SS_PAINTED_*), wall masking above cap rail required for BOTH methods.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: NC may have subfloor during wainscot painting. Finished/partial floors require drop cloth runners.
Rare in NC. Occupied sensitive triggers OCC_SENSITIVE modifier 1.30× on protection tasks per Modifier_Registry.

site_condition_rules.effect: Temperature affects dry times, open time, and flow-out. Particularly impacts waterborne alkyd at QT4+ which relies on extended open time.
site_condition_rules.notes: Refer to manufacturer PDS for temperature limits.

site_condition_rules.effect: MDF edge sealing uses solvent-based products — adequate ventilation required. Spray generates overspray requiring air movement.
site_condition_rules.notes: Poor ventilation extends dry times for all coats.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Wainscot panel painting is part of the millwork/trim package in NC. Typical project sequence: Prime ceilings → Prime walls → Finish ceilings → Trim/wainscot/window package → Wall finish. Wainscot pairs with SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT for shared finish group (cap rail, baseboard often same color/sheen).
sequencing_notes.internal_sequence: Single paintable item — no internal component sequencing needed. Spray technique within assembly: field panels first (broad passes), then frame detail (HVLP/fine tip).
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Floor protection → Wall masking (spray) → Apply coats → Teardown wall mask → Teardown floor drops → Vacuum.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-specific) → [MDF edge seal if bare MDF] → [Primer (conditional on SS_BARE)] → [Interstage] → Finish coat 1 → Interstage → Finish coat 2 → [QT5 brush: Interstage → Finish coat 3] → Final inspect → Cleanup

relationships.notes: Wainscot painting is part of the trim package in NC. Same crew, same material system, same session as other trim. Cap rail and baseboard typically painted in same session as wainscot panels.

sections_used: §4 — Primer Systems (MDF edge seal, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block)
§2 — Core Principles (primer is configuration, interstage is universal)
Height Modifiers (H1 for wainscot — always below waist height)
Modifier Application Rule (time multipliers, not rate multipliers)

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Dry times should be specified in specs
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: No dry times in specs — refer to product PDS.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Material system selection is mandatory doctrine
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Material systems are suggestions per QT — contractor has discretion.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Waterborne alkyds have longer open time
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Both Advance (waterborne alkyd) and Emerald Urethane (acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd) have SHORT working times.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC wainscot panel system painting (Spec #13 in Phase 3 catalog). Key features: combined prime+paint with conditional primer (substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish), single SF paintable item (ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL) covering entire assembly, wainscot_type configuration dimension (flat_panel/raised_panel/beadboard) with complexity modifiers (1.0×/1.25×/1.15×), 5 substrate-driven primer paths (MDF two-step, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard, plus factory-primed skip), 3 QT-driven finish systems (all reusing existing SYS_FF_* IDs), 3 caulk joint types in prep, H1 always (32-42 inch height), 25 SOP tasks across 7 modules, 3 round configurations, 2 protection zones, 9 variants. All material system IDs reuse existing entries — no new SYS_ IDs needed. Cap rail excluded — routed to SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.
